A_target.statement:
Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a [[Definition:Topological Space|topological space]].
Then:
:an arbitrary [[Definition:Set Intersection|intersection]] of [[Definition:Closed Set (Topology)|closed sets]] of $T$ is closed
:a finite [[Definition:Set Union|union]] of closed sets of $T$ is closed

B_source.statement:
Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a [[Definition:Topological Space|topological space]].
Then:
:an arbitrary [[Definition:Set Union|union]] of [[Definition:Open Set (Topology)|open sets]] of $T$ is open
:a finite [[Definition:Set Intersection|intersection]] of open sets of $T$ is open

derived.arbitrary union of opens is open: arbitrary intersection of closeds is closed
derived.finite intersection of opens is open: finite union of closeds is closed

object_map.reformulation: Take complements: a set is closed iff its complement is open, and apply De Morgan's laws to swap unions with intersections.

validity_conditions: Closed is defined as complement-of-open, so the correspondence is exact.
De Morgan's laws convert unions to intersections and vice versa under complementation, including the arbitrary/finite distinction which is preserved.
proof_plan: By {{Defof|Closed Set (Topology)}}, $F$ is closed {{iff}} its [[Definition:Relative Complement|complement]] $S \setminus F$ is open.

Let $\set {F_i: i \in I}$ be closed sets.
Then each $U_i = S \setminus F_i$ is [[Definition:Open Set (Topology)|open]].
By the [[Definition:Topology|open set axioms]], $\displaystyle \bigcup_{i \mathop \in I} U_i$ is open, and for finite $I$, $\displaystyle \bigcap_{i \mathop \in I} U_i$ is open.
